last_line_sync.note: NOT a regeneration. Only the `line` field of already-present entries was updated; every entry's (severity, code, file, message) identity was preserved 1:1. The sync aborts rather than writing if any identity would be added or dropped, so a genuine new violation cannot be absorbed by this operation. Root cause of the drift: the 2026-08-05 baseline was generated against a tree state 3 lines shorter than origin/main (a uniform +3 shift affects 94 entries on files otherwise untouched by this branch), plus a +44 shift in tests/integration/helpers.zig from the ISS-0137 test-wiring commit baea783. Verified: zero findings changed identity, so BLOCKER count is unchanged at 88 both before and after.
last_line_sync.t020_helpers_decision: The 3 T020 MAJORs on tests/integration/helpers.zig (`cached_owner_tag`:388, `tag_repr_storage`:393, `tag_repr_lock`:394) were each reviewed individually and DELIBERATELY KEPT BASELINED rather than fixed in source. These three module-level vars are the intended mechanism of ISS-0602 / GH #414 (commit 316d350, 'scope killIdleConnections by per-process owner tag'): an initialise-once, lock-guarded, process-lifetime cache of the per-process owner tag. T020 flags module-level `var` because shared mutable state normally leaks between test blocks, but here the cross-block sharing IS the required semantics -- killIdleConnections must scope by a tag that is stable for the whole process, and ownership is explicitly transferred to the first TestHarness via `owns_tag_storage` and freed in its deinit (helpers.zig:1084-1091). Making them per-test would reintroduce the ISS-0602 failure mode of one test binary killing another's connections. Access is guarded by tag_repr_lock's cmpxchg spinlock with acquire/release ordering, so the shared state is race-free. These entries were already present in the 2026-08-05 baseline at lines 344/349/350; only their line numbers were stale.
